title: Exercise 3 – Nintendo and the capital market line
text: Your friend currently invests all his savings in a single stock, Nintendo. Nintendo has an expected return of 10% and a volatility of 40%. The market portfolio has an expected return of 8% and a volatility of 16%. The risk-free return is 4%. Assume that the CAPM holds.

title: Exercise 4 – Expected market return
text: Assume that the S&P 500 index currently has a dividend yield of 4%, that the dividends of S&P 500 firms have increased by about 2% per year on average, and that the risk-free rate is 1%.

title: Exercise 5 – EduHos Inc
text: EduHos Inc is a conglomerate with two divisions: a for-profit university and a for-profit hospital. Its market capitalization is EUR 300 million and it has EUR 200 million of debt. Shareholders require a return of 7% per year; the debt holders require 3% and the debt can be considered risk-free. Assume perfect capital markets.

title: Exercise 6 – Hexa and Octo (replaces the IPO auction)
text: Hexa Industries and Octo Systems have identical assets that generate identical cash flows. Hexa is all-equity financed with 8 million shares trading at EUR 30. Octo has 12 million shares and EUR 60 million of debt. Assume perfect capital markets.
